slice: R1 browser-side canonical Context Pack bounds remediation

trigger.closed_gap: Outgoing Work authoring drafts now enforce the canonical per-field, count, exact-reference, Unicode, and aggregate UTF-8 byte limits before any request is sent.

closed_assertions.code_points: Summary, fact statements, and questions use Unicode code-point counts matching Python len on valid Unicode scalar text, rather than UTF-16 code units.
closed_assertions.counts: The browser enforces at most 64 facts, 8 exact sources per fact, 32 decisions, and 32 open questions.
closed_assertions.references: Source and decision references retain the closed kind and typed-ID grammar and reject duplicates before submission.
closed_assertions.canonical_bytes: The browser sorts the fixed semantic JSON keys and applies compact UTF-8 encoding equivalent to canonical_json_bytes before enforcing the 65,536-byte ceiling.
closed_assertions.network_boundary: An oversized outgoing draft raises a typed local validation result and does not call fetch.
closed_assertions.feedback: Every local refusal has paired actionable English and Russian copy; the form also states all canonical limits.
closed_assertions.privacy: No provider output, prompt, reasoning, transcript, credentials, or shared authority is recorded or exposed.

verification.canonical_byte_parity: Browser byte counts 261 and 248 match Python canonical_json_bytes for fixed ASCII and escaped/multibyte fixtures.
